headline: 1 sentenced to death, 3 to life in MC College gang rape case
summary: A Sylhet court has delivered a verdict in a 2020 case where a woman was gang raped at a college hostel after her husband was held captive.
details: A Sylhet Speedy Trial Tribunal judge sentenced Saifur Rahman to death and three others—Shah Mahbubur Rahman alias Rony, Tarekul Islam alias Tarek, and Arjun Laskar—to life imprisonment.
The convicts, identified as leaders and activists of the now-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League, were present in court during the verdict.
Four other accused individuals were acquitted due to a lack of evidence.
The incident occurred on September 25, 2020, when a group of youths intercepted a couple's car in front of the main gate of MC College.
The attackers took the couple to the college hostel, confined the husband, and gang raped the woman while assaulting both of them.
The couple was also robbed of their cash, valuables, and their vehicle.
The court's decision followed the testimony of 24 witnesses, including the survivor, her husband, and forensic experts.
Tight security was deployed around the court premises to maintain order during the verdict delivery.
caption:
One man faces the death penalty and three others receive life sentences for a brutal gang rape at MC College.

A Sylhet Speedy Trial Tribunal judge sentenced Saifur Rahman to death and three others—Shah Mahbubur Rahman alias Rony, Tarekul Islam alias Tarek, and Arjun Laskar—to life imprisonment.

The convicts, identified as leaders and activists of the now-banned Bangladesh Chhatra League, were present in court during the verdict.

Four other accused individuals were acquitted due to a lack of evidence.

The incident occurred on September 25, 2020, when a group of youths intercepted a couple's car in front of the main gate of MC College.

The attackers took the couple to the college hostel, confined the husband, and gang raped the woman while assaulting both of them.

The couple was also robbed of their cash, valuables, and their vehicle.

The court's decision followed the testimony of 24 witnesses, including the survivor, her husband, and forensic experts.

Tight security was deployed around the court premises to maintain order during the verdict delivery.

headline: 31 dead as landslides and floods hit Cox's Bazar
summary: The disasters have caused 31 deaths and an estimated 46 crore BDT loss in the fisheries sector alone.
details: Heavy rainfall has triggered devastating landslides and floods in Cox's Bazar, resulting in the death of 31 people.
The natural disasters have caused widespread destruction across the region, affecting thousands of residents and their livelihoods.
The fisheries sector has been hit particularly hard, with estimated losses amounting to 46 crore BDT.
Local authorities are working to manage the crisis as the region continues to recover from the sudden environmental impact.
